description: GradeThread is an AI-powered SaaS platform providing standardized condition grading for pre-owned clothing. Sellers submit structured photos of garments and receive a numerical condition grade (CG 1.0-10.0), a detailed condition report, and a shareable grade certificate. The platform addresses the trust gap in the $350B+ secondhand clothing market. Tech stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite frontend, self-hosted Supabase (api.gradethread.com) for auth/DB/storage, Deno/Hono edge functions for backend API, Claude Vision AI for grading, Stripe for payments, Cloudflare Pages for hosting. Brand colors: Navy #0F3460, Red #E94560, Night #1A1A2E, Soft Gray #F5F5F5. Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui (New York style). The platform includes full inventory management with financial tracking from acquisition through sale and shipment, detailed financial reporting and analytics, and a comprehensive admin panel for user management, traffic monitoring, and AI model self-refinement.

A running production edge therefore implies the DB is at 00474 or AHEAD, i.e. 00332-00474 are applied. userStories.title: Thrift Radar: aggregation engine + k-anonymity floor
userStories.description: As the Radar system, I need scheduled aggregation that turns anonymized scan events into venue-level intelligence (brand density, grade quality, freshness) that is only ever served above an anonymity floor.

Read-only edge endpoint serves aggregates (venue list by bounding box + venue detail); responses contain no per-user or per-contributor data.
deno tests cover the aggregation math, k-floor enforcement, and retention pruning; migration follows the US-1108 triple.

userStories.title: Cross-browser: Firefox + Edge support for the unified extension
userStories.description: As a Firefox or Edge user, I want the extension to work. Audit: both extensions are Chrome-only in practice — background declares only service_worker (Firefox MV3 runs event pages via background.scripts; with only service_worker Firefox loads NO background at all); no browser_specific_settings.gecko.id (AMO requires it); the Lister additionally awaits promise-style chrome.* APIs that are callback-only on Firefox, and its onMessageExternal registration would throw at top level there. Edge is Chromium-compatible as-is and only needs a store submission.
acceptanceCriteria: Manifest declares BOTH background.service_worker and background.scripts (the documented cross-browser pattern) + browser_specific_settings.gecko { id, strict_min_version: '109.0' }

A small runtime shim guarantees promise-style APIs on both browsers (use the browser.* namespace where present, or wrap the needed chrome.* calls); no top-level listener registration can throw on a browser lacking the event (guard onMessageExternal existence)

The research surface (condition read) works end-to-end on Firefox: config fetch, grade call (README's moz-extension origin in EXTENSION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS documented in .env.example), overlay, popup, storage — verified manually on a real listing; Firefox's opt-in host-permissions flow is handled (prompt or graceful degradation)
Seller tools on Firefox: explicitly gated OFF with honest UI copy until US-1882 lands (externally_connectable does not exist on Firefox — no silent breakage)
Edge: the unified build loads and passes a manual smoke on Edge; store packaging checklist (Edge Add-ons) appended to US-1757's distribution scope

userStories.title: Web↔extension transport v2: postMessage bridge so seller tools work beyond Chromium
userStories.description: As a Firefox (later Safari) seller, I want 'Send to extension' to work. The current transport is chrome.runtime.sendMessage from the page via externally_connectable — Chromium-only by platform design. The standard alternative is a gradethread.com content script relaying window.postMessage to the background.
acceptanceCriteria: The unified extension adds a gradethread.com content script that relays a versioned, origin-checked window.postMessage protocol to the background (message schema validated exactly like the current external messages; responses relayed back with correlation ids)

src/lib/lister-extension.ts feature-detects transports: externally_connectable where available, postMessage bridge otherwise; isListerAvailable() reflects either; timeouts/settled-guard semantics preserved

Security parity: the bridge accepts messages only from window.top on allowed origins, validates payloads with the same schema, and never exposes marketplace responses to the page beyond the current result shape; the privacy copy (US-1872) already covers the gradethread.com host permission this requires
Chromium keeps using externally_connectable (no regression); Firefox seller flows verified end-to-end on Poshmark
userStories.notes: Unblocks the Firefox seller half of US-1881. The gradethread.com content script is the deliberate privacy-posture trade the US-1872 epic documents. | 2026-07-18 (agent loop): STATUS WAS STALE — this story read as unstarted but the bridge had already shipped (extension-unified/gt-bridge.js), which is why US-1881's notes referred to it as landed. Audited all four ACs against the code rather than the status. AC1 DONE: gt-bridge.js is a document_start content script on gradethread.com relaying a versioned envelope ({__gtExtReq,id,message} -> runtime.sendMessage -> {__gtExtRes,id,response}) with correlation ids, a `replied` guard covering Chrome's callback and Firefox's promise return, and responses posted to an EXPLICIT target origin (never '*'). AC2 DONE: src/lib/lister-extension.ts:406 feature-detects — externally_connectable when chrome.runtime+id are present, else sendViaBridge; isListerAvailable() accepts the DOM marker alone (no extension id needed); the EXTENSION_TIMEOUT_MS backstop, the pushWaiters settled-guard and the deliberate do-not-settle-on-transportError semantics (MV3 worker-death cover) are all preserved. AC4 (Chromium no-regression) verified in code: the manifest still declares externally_connectable, sendViaRuntime is still PREFERRED, and both transports converge on the same handleExternalMessage which re-checks the sender origin via GT_LISTER_GUARD.isOriginAllowed. GAP FOUND AND CLOSED (AC3): the AC requires the bridge accept messages 'only from window.top on allowed origins'. The origin half was satisfied (the content script only runs on gradethread.com, event.source!==window rejects other windows, and the background re-checks origin), but there was NO framing guard. The threat is clickjacking rather than forgery — event.source!==window already means only same-frame scripts can send an envelope and a cross-origin parent can run none — but a framed gradethread.com would let the page's OWN 'Send to extension' control be clicked through by a victim who cannot see it: a genuine seller action from a real click. gt-bridge.js now returns immediately unless window.top === window, installing NO marker and NO listeners (a marker alone would make the page offer seller UI in a context the extension refuses to serve), and fails CLOSED when reading window.top throws, which is what a cross-origin frame does. ⚠ NOTE this is defense in depth, not a live hole: gradethread.com ships X-Frame-Options: DENY and CSP frame-ancestors 'none' — VERIFIED LIVE on the zone this pass. It is in the extension anyway because an extension must not stake its security on a response header it does not control; headers get relaxed for a partner embed or a preview host and the guarantee would vanish with nothing failing to signal it. TESTS: new extension-unified/test/gt-bridge.test.cjs EXECUTES the bridge against a stubbed window/document (rather than grepping source) and asserts: top-level installs marker+listener; framed installs NEITHER; a throwing cross-origin window.top also fails closed; the relay round-trips a correlation id and posts to an explicit origin; five malformed/foreign envelopes are ignored; and the background->page push relay forwards ONLY GT_LISTER_JOB_UPDATE/GT_LISTER_LISTED, never arbitrary background traffic. Both new guarantees negative-verified (removing the frame guard, and widening the push allowlist, each turn the suite red). 13/13 extension test files; packager still emits a valid FF zip. KEPT passes:false ON AC4 ONLY: 'Firefox seller flows verified end-to-end on Poshmark' needs a real browser on a real marketplace — same browser-gate as US-1881 AC3/AC5, and not something this agent can do. Everything else in the story is code-complete and tested.

userStories.title: Listing Quality Score: one 0–100 number per listing aggregating every verified ranking lever
userStories.description: As a seller, I want a single score telling me how well each listing plays eBay's actual ranking game — and exactly which fix earns the most points — so optimizing 300 drafts stops requiring SEO knowledge. Audit: no listing-quality score exists anywhere (verified against current prd + archive); components exist piecemeal (aspect blockers, compliance card, category nudge).
acceptanceCriteria: Edge lib computes score + component breakdown from verified levers only: title quality (US-1890 lint + utilization), required+recommended aspect coverage (US-1895 math), photo standards (US-1896 data: count, hero type, dimensions), category confidence (leaf + suggestion match), condition-tier/description consistency (US-1894), and fulfillment signals read from the listing's resolved business policies (returns accepted, ≤1-day handling, free-shipping) — weights documented in the lib with playbook citations

Returned in the validate/preflight response and persisted on the listing row for sorting; drafts list + pipeline board show the score with a breakdown popover where each component links to its fix surface
Score never invents folklore signals (no Best Offer, no relist-freshness); copy for fulfillment components cites 'eBay Best Match factors'
Deno tests: component fixtures produce expected scores; a fully-optimized fixture scores 100

iOS surfaces the same score: PublishDialog shows the score + component breakdown (each component naming its fix surface) read from the validate/preflight response the app already calls, and drafts-library rows show a score chip usable for sorting — no client-side recomputation of weights (parity audit 2026-07-09: original criteria covered only the web drafts list + pipeline board)
userStories.notes: [P2][SEO][Capstone] Depends on US-1890/1894/1895/1896 landing first (build after them). See EBAY_RANKING_PLAYBOOK.md. Added 2026-07-09. | PARTIAL 2026-07-18 (agent loop — story stays passes:false). Dependencies confirmed landed first (US-1890/1894/1895/1896 + US-1490 all archived passes:true), so the capstone is genuinely unblocked. DONE: AC1 scoring lib + AC3 + AC4. New lib/listing-quality-score.ts — pure, every input supplied by the caller because assemblePublishContext already computes all six signals in one pass. Weights sum to 100 and each cites its EBAY_RANKING_PLAYBOOK.md section: aspects 30 (§1 'single highest-confidence lever'), photos 25 (§6 thumbnail = 'biggest CTR lever'), title 15, category 12, fulfillment 10 (§4 eBay-CONFIRMED returns/≤1-day handling/free shipping), condition 8. The playbook publishes NO numbers deliberately, so the values are a judgement call but the ORDERING is not — a test pins aspects > photos > title > fulfillment. New lib/business-policy-signals.ts closes the gap the audit found: PolicySet carries only policy IDs, but syncBusinessPolicies already writes eBay's ENTIRE raw policy object into business_policies.policy_data, so the three fulfillment signals are parsed from that jsonb — nothing new is fetched. handlingTime is normalised across DAY/BUSINESS_DAY/HOUR (24h == 1 day, since rejecting it would under-score a seller who IS meeting the bar); free shipping accepts both the explicit flag and a zero shippingCost; a free INTERNATIONAL service does not count (Best Match ranks for the buyers being served). Everything fails to null, never false — 'unreadable policy' and 'seller refuses returns' are different facts and collapsing them would tell a seller to fix something already correct. AC3 (no folklore) drove a real design call. AC1's phrase 'title … utilization' invites rewarding titles near 80 chars — which is EXACTLY the vendor lore §2 flags as not an eBay statement. So title scores policy cleanliness (US-1890, a real blocker) plus a floor below which there is too little searchable text to match queries; there is no optimal band and no positional weighting. Tests assert 68 vs 78 chars TIE and that word order never moves the score, plus a guard that no component string mentions Best Offer / relist / Sell Similar / stemming / templates (§10 non-factors). TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS worth reviewing, both made after eyeballing the score across realistic listings rather than trusting green tests: (1) BLOCKED_SCORE_CEILING — the purely additive score LIED about exactly the listings a seller most needs to find: one missing required specific scored 70 and a non-leaf category scored 88, both for listings eBay refuses to list at all, so triaging 300 drafts by score would sort them into the 'fine' pile. Any publish-blocking component (no title, title policy violation, missing required aspect, no photos, sub-500px hero, non-leaf/not-found category) now caps the whole score at 40 and sets blocked + blockingReasons. A test asserts a blocked listing sorts BELOW the worst publishable one, and another asserts merely-weak listings are NOT marked blocked (a seller must be able to tell 'will not list' from 'will list badly'). (2) the aspects component was rebalanced from required 55%/recommended 45% to 25%/75% — paying most of the component for having no MISSING required aspect is paying for table stakes (it is a blocker otherwise), and it left recommended coverage barely moving the number (2/8 filled still scored 80; now 74). Unknown signals are excluded from BOTH numerator and denominator and the score rescales, so an unsynced business policy cannot drag a perfect listing below 100 — the score must not drift with OUR sync health. Verified: 25 tests in listing-quality-score_test.ts; full edge suite 4124 passed / 0 failed; deno lint (1168 files); deno check src/main.ts. NOT DONE (blocks passes): AC2 — the score is NOT yet returned from POST /listings/validate (the natural home is PublishContextOk in flipdesk-ebay.ts, which already computes every input) and NOT persisted on the listing row for sorting; persistence needs a migration + the drafts list / pipeline board breakdown popover. AC5 — iOS PublishDialog + drafts-library score chip; cannot be built or tested on Windows (Swift/xcodebuild is macOS-only). userStories.description: As an established reseller onboarding to GradeThread, I want to manage my existing eBay listings, not just view them. Today Trading-created listings import read-only (getAllActiveEbaySelling) and relist explicitly refuses eBay-origin, so a new customer's live catalog can never be revised/repriced/promoted through GradeThread — a major onboarding wall. userStories.notes: [P2][Edge/Inventory] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No bulkMigrateListing anywhere; relist refuses origin==='ebay' (flipdesk-ebay.ts:6503). See SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md — migration changes a mirror into a GT-managed listing. Unlocks managing existing catalogs (most customers' day one). | INVESTIGATION 2026-07-17 (no code): AC2's PROMISE WOULD BE SILENTLY FALSE without an unstated design decision. GOOD NEWS FIRST: AC2's 'flip to a managed origin' needs NO migration — listing_origin is already an enum with both values (00232) and deriveListingOrigin() lets a persisted marker WIN over the provenance signals (sync-precedence.ts:330), so setting listing_origin='gradethread' does unlock revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote. THE PROBLEM IS THE SKU. bulkMigrateListing returns eBay's OWN sku + offerId per listing (inventoryItems[{sku,offerId}], max 5 listings/call, per-listing statusCode + errors[] — verified against eBay docs). The Inventory API keys EVERYTHING on that sku. But nothing in GradeThread stores a per-listing sku: BOTH the publish path (flipdesk-ebay.ts:8733) and the revise/list path (:9450) DERIVE it as (item.sku)?.trim() || 'FD-'+id.slice(0,8). So if eBay's migrated sku differs from our derived one — likely, since eBay derives it from the listing's Custom Label or generates it — then after a 'successful' migration every subsequent GT Inventory call targets an inventory item that does not exist, and revise/reprice/withdraw all fail. userStories.notes: [P1][Sync/SEO][Regression of an ARCHIVED story] Found 2026-07-18 by the unwired-export audit that also produced US-1994. Do NOT just import the module in an edge route and call it — see AC2/AC3; the double-apply and needs_review semantics are the hard part, not the substitution. Meanwhile the edge module carries a ⚠ header naming the gap so its green tests stop reading as proof the feature works server-side. | 2026-07-18 (cont.): the audit is now a repeatable tool — scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs. Re-running it correctly found 10 WHOLE MODULES that no production file imports, carrying 143 test references between them: drip-trigger.ts (4 exports/31 refs — US-933s unified trigger engine, SUPERSEDED by the inline switch(journey.trigger) in jobs-journey-tick.ts, so dead rather than broken), title-sync.ts (4/29 — this story), authenticity-eval.ts (6/24), measure-eval-stats.ts (3/16 — the MeasureCard accuracy gate, plausibly just pending its OPEN story US-1582), ai-size-estimate-core.ts (3/15), brand-seed.ts (2/12), grading-reliability.ts (2/11), grade-badge.ts (1/5), content-ai-email.ts (4/0), rubric.ts (1/0). NOTE the tool initially MISSED title-sync.ts — the module that motivated it — because its exports call each other (syncTitle uses applyTitleSubstitution), so per-function reference counting read internal cohesion as reachability. Whole-module deadness is now decided by the IMPORT GRAPH, which is the only signal that cannot be faked from inside the module. | 2026-07-18 SCOPE CORRECTED — MY OWN FRAMING WAS WRONG. This story (and its first AC) assumed 'the edge item update path' exists. IT DOES NOT: there is no generic item-update endpoint anywhere in services/edge-functions — no route does .update() on inventory_items. A seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts gets 40 stale titles, and that is the exact bug US-1891 was written to kill. AND THE REAL QUESTION IS ARCHITECTURAL, not a wiring task: with writes distributed across five+ surfaces in three languages, per-surface mirrors do not converge — that is how there came to be two copies of title-sync with only one wired. The decision to make FIRST is WHERE THE INVARIANT LIVES: a DB trigger on inventory_items (fires for every writer, including iOS and any future one), funnelling item writes through a single edge endpoint (large change, but kills the whole class), or accepting per-surface mirrors with a shared behavioural fixture as the guard. It imports title-sync zero times; item-canvas.tsx imports it three. So IF the chosen answer is per-surface mirrors, this specific fix is roughly 'call changesFromItemDiff + syncTitle in the existing patch loop', not a new data path. I DELIBERATELY DID NOT MAKE THAT CHANGE. This same note argues scattered per-surface call sites are the disease — two copies of title-sync with one wired — so adding a fifth call site before the where-does-the-invariant-live decision would be inconsistent with the advice above, and wasted work if the answer turns out to be a DB trigger on inventory_items (which would cover iOS and every future writer for free).
